panel1.note: Post-2021 master lease restructuring (IDR denomination) and Dec 2020 rights issue diluted DPU from 4.15¢ in FY20 to 2.61¢.
Supported by initial rental contribution from 12 Japan nursing homes acquired in March 2022.
Depreciation of Indonesian Rupiah and Japanese Yen against SGD began outweighing 4.5% local-currency base rent escalations.
Sustained FX translation drag eroded SGD distributable income despite resilient local-currency hospital performance.
Cumulative 16.9% DPU erosion over 5 years from FY21 (2.61¢ to 2.17¢) driven by IDR depreciation and higher financing costs.
Pro forma assuming Jan 1, 2025 Tranche 1 exit: recurring DPU drops from 2.17¢ to 1.39¢, partially cushioned by 0.46¢ special dividend (S$9.7m surplus).
Annualised from 9M26 DPU of 1.44¢ (3Q26: 0.46¢). Hurt by 8.0% IDR and 9.8% JPY depreciation YoY plus initial divestment impact.
Total DPU projected to plunge 33% YoY to 1.24¢ (1.01¢ recurring + 0.23¢ 1Q27 final special payout) after losing 11 Indonesian properties.

panel2.note: Book value prior to the Dec 2020 recapitalisation rights issue (791.1m new units issued on a 98-for-100 basis at S$0.20/unit).
Sharp dilution from rights issue and master lease restructuring valuation reset.
431.1m new units issued at S$0.305/unit to sponsor OUE Lippo Healthcare for Japan acquisition; total units expanded 2.55x from Dec 2019 to Dec 2022.
IDR and JPY weakness against SGD reduced translated investment property values.
Total AUM contracted to S$1,022.6m (from S$1,139.5m in FY23) due to foreign exchange translation losses.
AUM declined further to S$962.4m (74.5% Indonesia, 22.7% Japan, 2.8% Singapore) amid persistent IDR depreciation.
11 Indonesian properties (~S$450m) reclassified as held for sale; unitholders' funds dropped to S$487.4m.
NAV fell to 20.94¢ following Tranche 1 completion (24 Sep 2026) due to divestment-related transaction costs and currency depreciation.

panel3.note: Healthy leverage baseline after S$158.2m Dec 2020 rights issue proceeds pared down debt.
Total debt reached S$461.2m following acquisition of 12 Japan nursing homes and early loan refinancing.
Debt remained stable while FX headwinds began compressing the SGD denominator of total deposited property.
Gearing approached 40% as IDR and JPY depreciation reduced SGD portfolio valuation to S$1,022.6m.
Total debt stood at S$458.0m against shrinking AUM (S$962.4m); all-in cost of debt at 4.5% and ICR at 3.7x.
Total debt hit S$469.6m while FX eroded asset values, forcing a pre-emptive financial covenant waiver (May–Jul 2026) and CGIF bond consent solicitation.
Tranche 1 proceeds (S$471.5m received 24 Sep 2026) deployed to repay S$300m loan facilities and JPY Shinsei social loan.
Pro forma after full redemption of S$100m 3.25% CGIF-Guaranteed Bonds on 19 Oct 2026. All-in cost of debt improved to 3.9% and ICR rose to 4.2x.

tooltip.title: Indonesia Healthcare Portfolio (Divested)
tooltip.note: CEO Victor Tan & Chairman confirmed at the April 2026 AGM that the +3.0% net spread was completely wiped out by a ~10% annual IDR currency depreciation loss.

tooltip.title: Japan Nursing Homes (Primary Target Market)
rows: Local JPY Debt Cost (2.0%–2.5% AGM range):
tooltip.note: Debt-funded acquisitions net only ~1.60% cash yield after REIT management fees and trust/tax expenses, while still exposing unitholders to JPY depreciation (-22.9% SGD valuation drop from FY22 to 3Q26).

tooltip.title: Australia Healthcare Properties
tooltip.note: At the April 2026 AGM, CEO Victor Tan disclosed that Australian base rates (4.1%) plus bank margins (1.5%–2.0%) push borrowing costs to 5%–6%, matching 5%–6% property yields and leaving zero debt carry.

tooltip.title: Singapore Nursing Homes (3 Legacy Assets)
tooltip.note: CEO Victor Tan clarified at the April 2026 AGM that First REIT’s 3 Singapore properties have short remaining land tenures (decaying toward zero in 5.5–10.8 years) and are non-comparable to scarce standard Singapore healthcare acquisitions (4%–5% yield).

tooltip.title: FY2025 Actual Baseline (Pre-Divestment)
tooltip.note: Indonesia contributed 82.5% (S$82.9m) of gross rental income across 14 properties prior to the proposed two-tranche divestment.

tooltip.title: Lost Tranche 1 Net Property Cash Flow
tooltip.note: Selling the 11 Tranche 1 Indonesian properties removes S$35.26m of net property cash flow (after Indonesian withholding and corporate taxes), creating a S$16.46m net hole even after debt interest savings.

tooltip.title: Pro Forma Annual Interest Expense Savings
tooltip.note: Repaying the CGIF bonds, SBLC, and S$300m facility saves S$18.80m annually (5.18% implied all-in debt cost), offsetting only 53.3% of the lost Indonesian property cash flow.

tooltip.title: Post-Tranche 1 Recurring Run-Rate (Ex-Special)
tooltip.note: Excluding the one-off S$9.7m special distribution (0.46c/unit paid across two quarters), recurring DPU drops 35.9% from 2.17c to 1.39c.

tooltip.title: Hypothetical S$360m Japan Nursing Home Acquisition
tooltip.note: Deploying S$80m Tranche 1 cash + S$280m JPY debt pushes gearing back to 42.1% (on S$890m AUM) yet recovers only 45.9% of the S$16.46m shortfall. Fully closing the gap in Japan would require S$916m of acquisitions (breaching MAS’s 50% gearing cap).

tooltip.title: Reconstituted Portfolio Run-Rate (Back at 42.1% Gearing)
tooltip.note: Even after exhausting debt headroom back to 42.1% leverage in Japan, compressed developed-market yield spreads leave a permanent 19.5% DPU shortfall.
